speaker: Patient
text: The headaches started two weeks ago and have been getting worse, especially in the mornings. speaker: Doctor
text: That is a significant finding; the presence of oligoclonal bands and elevated protein in the CSF strongly suggests an inflammatory process within the central nervous system. Have you noticed any new neurological deficits, such as weakness, numbness, or balance issues, accompanying these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't noticed any weakness, numbness, or trouble with my balance. My main issues are just the morning headaches and the visual disturbances you mentioned. speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple Sclerosis (relapsing-remitting). The combination of morning headaches, visual disturbances (likely optic neuritis), and the presence of oligoclonal bands in the CSF is classic for MS. I will proceed with ordering a Brain MRI to confirm demyelinating lesions.
